title: Live theatre evaluation
examples: How do I tell if a performance was good or bad?
What should I look for when watching a play?
Can you give me tips for writing a theatre review?

explain.say: Today we will learn to evaluate a live theatre performance. This means giving thoughtful feedback on what you saw.
First we look at the acting. We should notice how the actors use their voices and bodies. A strong performance uses clear vocal projection.
Next we analyse the design elements. This includes the set, the costumes, and the lighting. These things create the world of the play.
We must also consider the script itself. Think about the writing and the characters' motivations. Does the story make sense overall?
In real life, you might evaluate a local community play. You could write a review for the school newsletter about it.
A common mistake is just saying if you liked it or not. You must explain why you feel that way using evidence from the show.

faq.q: What is the difference between analysing and evaluating?
faq.a: Analysing means breaking the performance down into parts to see how they work. Evaluating means making a judgment about the quality of those parts.
asks: What's the difference between describing and judging?
Do I just list things or do I judge them?

faq.q: Should I focus more on the acting or the design?
faq.a: You should balance your critique. Give equal attention to both the performers and the technical elements like lighting and set.
asks: Is acting more important than costumes?
How much time should I spend on different elements?

faq.a: It means making your voice loud enough so that everyone in the theatre can hear you clearly. It is about volume and clarity.
asks: What does good voice work mean?
How do I sound louder without shouting?

faq.q: What makes a set design effective?
faq.a: An effective set design supports the story and the mood. It should look believable for the time and place the play is set.
asks: Should the set be realistic or abstract?
Does the set need to look expensive?

faq.q: How do I structure my written evaluation?
faq.a: A good structure introduces the play, discusses specific elements with examples, and concludes with a final judgment.
asks: What order should I write my review in?
Do I need an introduction paragraph?

facts: Evaluation requires using specific evidence from the performance to support your claims.
Design elements like lighting and costumes help establish the mood or atmosphere.
Analyzing acting involves commenting on vocal choices and physical expression.
A strong critique balances positive observations with constructive criticism.

quiz.say: If you notice the lighting is too dim, which element are you analysing?
quiz.why: Lighting is a technical design element that contributes to the overall look and feel of the performance.

wrong.0: The script is the written text, not the physical lighting setup.
wrong.1: Plot relates to the sequence of events in the story.
wrong.3: Acting refers to the performers' voices and bodies, not the lights.

quiz.say: When evaluating, what is the best approach to giving feedback?

options.show: Pointing out a specific moment that worked well.
options.say: Pointing out a specific moment that worked well.

quiz.why: Good evaluation always points to a specific moment or example to back up your general statement.

wrong.1: This is too vague and does not help the audience understand why.
wrong.2: A balanced critique should also mention areas for improvement.
wrong.3: Focus your critique only on the performance you actually watched.

quiz.say: If an actor speaks very quietly, you are critiquing their:
quiz.why: Vocal projection is a core skill within the analysis of an actor's performance.

wrong.0: Pacing describes the speed of the action, not the volume of the voice.
wrong.2: Set design refers to the physical background items on stage.
wrong.3: Costume relates only to the clothing worn by the character.
